PBPK evaluation report — Dapagliflozin

⚠ POOR FIT — overall GMFE 2.468 (>2-fold typical error). The model is not yet an adequate description of the data.

1. Objective

Build a whole-body PBPK model for Dapagliflozin that reproduces the observed plasma concentration-time data. Decide the model structure and any parameters you cannot obtain from the given data, and justify them. No modeling strategy and no reference results are provided.

Background. Dapagliflozin PBPK modeling task.

Known biology:
  • Metabolized by: Hepatic-CYP, UGT1A9, UGT2B7.
  • Renal clearance via glomerular filtration is present.
  • Reference distribution/permeability methods exist but are withheld; choose your own.

3. Model & model choice

Distribution / permeability: Cellular partition coefficient method - PK-Sim Standard, Cellular permeability - PK-Sim Standard
Processes: UGT1A9, UGT2B7, GlomerularFiltration, Hepatic-CYP

Distribution was described with Cellular partition coefficient method - PK-Sim Standard, Cellular permeability - PK-Sim Standard. The active processes were UGT1A9, UGT2B7, GlomerularFiltration, Hepatic-CYP. Parameters that cannot be reliably transferred from in-vitro to in-vivo were estimated against the clinical data; measured physicochemical inputs were fixed.

4. Model equations (ODE system)

PK-Sim's standard human whole-body structure: ~15 perfused organs (lung, brain, heart, kidney, gut, spleen, pancreas, liver, stomach, muscle, skin, bone, adipose, gonads) plus arterial and venous blood pools. Each organ is further divided into plasma, blood-cell, interstitial and intracellular sub-compartments, so the solved system is one mass-balance ODE per sub-compartment (order ~10^2 states). The physiological volumes V and flows Q are fixed by the individual; only the drug terms below are model choices.

Perfused tissue (distribution)
V_t · dC_t/dt = Q_t · ( C_art − C_t / (K_p,t / R_bp) )
Each non-eliminating organ t (brain, heart, muscle, skin, adipose, bone, ...): rate in from arterial blood at flow Q_t, rate out with the venous effluent in equilibrium with tissue via the tissue:plasma partition coefficient K_p,t (R_bp = blood:plasma ratio).
Venous blood pool
V_ven · dC_ven/dt = Σ_t Q_t · C_t / (K_p,t / R_bp) − Q_co · C_ven + R_iv(t)
Collects the effluent of every organ; Q_co = cardiac output. IV doses enter here as an input rate R_iv(t) (bolus or infusion).
Arterial blood pool
V_art · dC_art/dt = Q_co · ( C_lung − C_art )
Blood is oxygenated/mixed through the lung and distributed to the organs.
Permeability-limited exchange (cellular)
V_cell · dC_cell/dt = P · SA · ( f_u·C_int − f_u,cell·C_cell / K_p,t )
Where cellular permeability limits uptake, the intracellular space is a separate state exchanging with interstitium across the membrane (permeability P × surface area SA), driven by the unbound gradient.
Liver (hepatic metabolism)
V_liv · dC_liv/dt = Q_liv·C_art + Q_po·C_po − Q_hv·C_liv/(K_p,liv/R_bp) − CL_int · f_u · C_liv
The liver receives arterial + portal (Q_po, first-pass) inflow; CYP3A4 metabolism removes drug as a first-order intrinsic-clearance sink CL_int·f_u·C_liv on the unbound concentration.
Kidney (renal filtration)
V_kid · dC_kid/dt = Q_kid·(C_art − C_kid/(K_p,kid/R_bp)) − GFR · f_u · C_kid
Glomerular filtration removes unbound drug at rate GFR·f_u·C_kid.
Oral absorption (PO doses)
dA_lum/dt = −P_int · SA_int · C_lum,u ;   J_abs = P_int · SA_int · C_lum,u  →  gut wall → portal vein → liver
Dissolved drug in the intestinal lumen permeates the mucosa (specific intestinal permeability P_int × surface area), enters the gut wall, and drains via the portal vein to the liver (first-pass).

Tissue partitioning. K_p,t is not a fitted number but is computed per organ from tissue composition by the PK-Sim Standard method — a function of effective lipophilicity, the unbound fraction f_u, drug ionization (pKa) and each tissue's lipid / water / phospholipid / protein content.

Where the fitted / fixed parameters enter:

  • Permeability — the cellular permeability P in the permeability-limited exchange term.
  • Lipophilicity (fixed) — sets every tissue partition coefficient K_p,t (the distribution terms in all organ ODEs).
  • Fraction unbound (plasma, reference value) (fixed) — f_u — scales every unbound-driven term (K_p,t, CL_int, GFR).
  • GFR fraction (fixed) — the renal filtration sink GFR in the kidney ODE.
  • Specific intestinal permeability (transcellular) (fixed) — P_int in the oral-absorption flux J_abs.

These are the governing equations; PK-Sim generates the fully instantiated system (every organ and sub-compartment, and the exact PK-Sim Standard K_p formula) at build time and integrates it numerically. The concentrations plotted are the peripheral-venous-plasma state.

Sensitivity = how much the fit responds to each estimated parameter, normalised to the most influential (1.0). A low value means the data weakly constrain that parameter, so its fitted value is uncertain.

6. Pharmacological rationale

Each estimated parameter, checked against independent literature where available: - CLspec/[Enzyme]@UGT1A9 = 0.3946 Sensitivity 1: well constrained by the data. - CLspec/[Enzyme]@UGT2B7 = 0.01885 Sensitivity 0.081 (of 1.0): the fit barely responds to this parameter — weakly identifiable, so its absolute value is uncertain. - Permeability = 2.89e-05 cm/min — within the physiological range [1e-06, 1.0]. Sensitivity 0.13: moderately constrained by the data.

8. Comparison with the ground-truth model

Post-hoc evaluation against the reference model (not seen during modeling). Each parameter is judged on both its distance from truth AND its identifiability: a value far from truth but weakly identified is not a real error, because the data cannot pin it.

Reference (published) overall GMFE: 1.413 vs this model 2.468.

Summary. The structure DIFFERS from the ground-truth model in: partition method. Overall fit is comparable (this model GMFE 2.468 vs reference 1.413). Of 8 compared parameters, 3 recovered well, 5 differ but are weakly identified / minor, and 0 are off despite being influential. 2 of the fitted parameters are collinear (trade off against a partner), so the data constrain their combination but not their individual values - the split needs an in-vitro anchor rather than more plasma data.

9. Conclusion

The model does NOT yet adequately reproduce the observed plasma concentrations: overall GMFE is 2.468 (beyond the ~2-fold typical error). This indicates a structural or parameter problem to resolve (check per-route bias and any parameters pinned to a bound) before the model can be considered fit for purpose.
